aiheet.nimi: Forces and the equation of motion

kortit.maaritelma: Where an object is in a chosen coordinate system at a given instant.
The total length of the path an object has travelled.
The change in an object's position, with its direction.
kortit.kaava_puhe: delta x equals x two minus x one

kortit.maaritelma: The rate of change of position, with the direction of motion.
The magnitude of the velocity, without its direction.
The whole displacement divided by the time it took.
kortit.kaava_puhe: v k is delta x divided by delta t

kortit.maaritelma: The velocity of an object at a given instant.
The velocity stays constant, so the position changes by equal amounts in equal time intervals.
Shows an object's position as a function of time.
A straight line that touches the curve at the point studied and gives the instantaneous rate of change.
On a position–time graph it gives the object's instantaneous velocity.
Shows an object's velocity as a function of time.
The signed area between the velocity–time graph and the time axis gives the displacement.
Shows an object's acceleration as a function of time.
The signed area under the acceleration–time graph gives the change in velocity.
A new graph of the rate of change is made from the slopes of a graph.
The rate of change of velocity.
kortit.kaava_puhe: a equals delta v divided by delta t

kortit.maaritelma: The total change in velocity divided by the time it took.
The rate of change of velocity at a given instant.
The acceleration stays the same, so the velocity changes steadily.
The velocity changes steadily with time.
kortit.kaava_puhe: v equals v nought plus a times t

kortit.maaritelma: The position follows from the initial position, the initial velocity and the acceleration.
kortit.kaava_puhe: x equals x nought plus v nought times t plus one half a t squared

kortit.maaritelma: The magnitude of the acceleration of a freely falling object near the Earth.
kortit.kaava_puhe: g is approximately 9.81 metres per second squared

kortit.maaritelma: Motion in which only the weight acts on the object and air resistance is neglected.
Something between two objects in which they can change each other's motion or shape.
Describes the strength of an interaction; its unit is the newton.
An object keeps its state of motion if the net force on it is zero; the law of inertia.
The property of an object to resist a change in its state of motion.
A net force gives an object an acceleration; the fundamental law of dynamics.
kortit.kaava_puhe: the sum of the forces equals m times a

kortit.maaritelma: The vector sum of the forces acting on an object.
In an interaction the objects exert equal but opposite forces on each other.
Two equal and opposite forces acting on different objects in the same interaction.
A drawing that shows every force acting on the object studied as an arrow.
The gravitational force the Earth exerts on an object.
The force a surface exerts on an object, perpendicular to the surface.
The force a taut string or rope exerts on an object, along the string.
Newton's second law applied: the sum of the forces on an object is linked to its acceleration.
The part of a force in a chosen direction of the coordinate system.
The equation of motion is written separately, for example in the horizontal and vertical directions.
In translational equilibrium the vector sum of the forces on an object is zero.
kortit.kaava_puhe: the sum of the forces is zero

kortit.maaritelma: The situation becomes easier when the axes are chosen along the plane and the forces are split into components.
A force between surfaces in contact that opposes their relative motion or the start of it.
Prevents surfaces from sliding over each other and adjusts to the size needed, up to its maximum.
Opposes the motion of surfaces sliding over each other (sliding friction).
kortit.kaava_puhe: F mu equals mu times N

kortit.maaritelma: A dimensionless number that depends on the pair of materials and describes the friction between the surfaces.
A gas or liquid exerts a force on a moving object that opposes its motion.
The drag force of the air on an object usually grows with the speed.
The constant velocity reached when the drag and the other forces along the motion cancel.
The upward force a liquid or gas exerts on an object.
A force transfers energy to or from an object during a displacement.
kortit.kaava_puhe: W equals F times s times cosine alpha

kortit.maaritelma: The energy of motion depends on the mass and the speed.
kortit.kaava_puhe: E k equals one half m v squared

kortit.maaritelma: The energy of a conservative interaction depends on the positions of the objects.
The energy related to gravity near the Earth.
kortit.kaava_puhe: E p equals m times g times h

kortit.maaritelma: The work done by the force depends only on the start and end positions, not on the path.
The sum of kinetic energy and potential energy.
kortit.kaava_puhe: E mech equals E k plus E p

kortit.maaritelma: In an isolated system the total energy stays constant.
Mechanical energy is conserved when only conservative forces do work.
The change in mechanical energy equals the work done by the non-conservative forces.
kortit.kaava_puhe: E p zero plus E k zero plus W equals E p plus E k

kortit.maaritelma: The work done by the net force on an object equals the change in its kinetic energy.
kortit.kaava_puhe: E k zero plus W equals E k

kortit.maaritelma: The product of an object's mass and velocity, a vector quantity.
Describes the total effect of a force over a time; for a constant force:
kortit.kaava_puhe: I equals F times delta t

kortit.maaritelma: The impulse an object receives equals the change in its momentum.
The area between the graph and the time axis gives the impulse the object receives.
The total momentum of an isolated system does not change in an interaction.
A short interaction in which the velocities and momenta of the objects can change quickly.
Besides the total momentum, the total kinetic energy of the objects is also conserved.
The total momentum is conserved, but part of the kinetic energy turns into other forms.
After the collision the objects move together at the same velocity.
The objects move along one line, so the directions of momentum can be handled with signs.
